result:
Worked by hand from the text alone; nothing was run. Five findings would change the freeze, so they come first.

## Findings that block the freeze

- **C: the serial law deadlocks the cycle of five (D2(5,3)) at depth 1 under every priority.** P3 fails on all seeds, and joins-first and offshoots-first cannot be told apart (working in 3).
- **A, gate: the CAP-4 clause is false.** Under the ordinary law a round-2 knot of Ring(5, 3) has demand 5, so CAP-4 binds.
- **A, P8 is likely false.** (CAP-4, CANCEL-WAIT) gives a returning part on Ring(5, 3) from round 3.
- **A6 is inert.** PART-CLOSE never fires without FILLERS, so A6 repeats A1.
- **An unnamed scaffold carries the result.** Step 5 lets a member that is not short spend, on offshoots, the distinctions its cancelled groups would have taken. That is what removes the offshoots and frees the waiting ring; if the member held them instead, the ring would wait for ever.

## 1. Definitions

**(a) Group rule.**
- "Contained in none of those sets" has three readings. Only "the groups of three or more just taken" reproduces 10, 15, 25 for Ring(5, 3); I checked round 3 as 5 triples plus 20 pairs. Say so in the text.
- Say that two witnesses with the same set give one group.
- A closing-exception join of two parents has two places, against "at least three places"; under parity that is an equality.

**(b) CANCEL-WAIT with step 6.**
- At positive age a new knot is never adjacent to a waiting member, so "with what it holds" does no work there. It matters only at source age.
- Step 6 counts every new knot as a member, which is false under FLOOR0 with three or more parents (it receives nothing) and inflates its siblings' demand.
- The release rule above belongs to this treatment and needs its own name and swap.

**(c) FILLERS.**
- A filler anywhere switches off the closing exception everywhere, which is a global coupling.
- A part that "ends" is left holding loose distinctions the law refuses to use. It has ended in the roster, not in the structure.
- Knots holding only never-used distinctions are live but not members, so "live roster" and the disclosed "live knots" counts are misnomers under the three rules.

**(d) Returns, gives parts off, in balance.**
- "Returns" needs positive age, so P9's "returns every round" cannot start from the ring itself.
- "Gives parts off" is read at round t only. "Comes apart" is used but never defined.
- T is "the period found" with no search order; say least s, then least t.
- A roster that waits for ever, or is empty, is "in balance" with period one. The outcome kinds are not exclusive, yet B2 records "the kind".
- Sameness sees only h, k and the maximal witnessed sets. That is enough for the round (I checked), but it should be stated as a lemma, because "the ring returns to its start" is true of the roster only.

**(e) Serial law.**
- Shortness is read again after every move, while in the round it is read once. This is the cause of the deadlock in 3.
- Shortness counts all open groups, but offshoot entitlement counts only groups free of short members. A knot can therefore make itself short by its own offshoot.
- DEPTH is a simulator's record, like OLDEST, unless parent direction is shown to be readable from the structure. The stop rule's "a priority read from the structure" overclaims.
- FEWEST-PLACES and MOST-LOOSE do not say which parent of a join is meant.
- C1 has no rule for "no move available".
- "Settled" never holds once a member is jammed, so "builds the same" is then false by default.
- "Build the same to depth D" does not say how a depth-D knot's distinctions held by deeper knots are treated. The definition also has no depth colours, while the hash does.
- A "ring part" needs the roster at positive age and every member holding three at one instant. Interleaving destroys that even when the built structure is identical.
- Under the DEAD witness rule the present-state count d is nearly always 0, because a parent is not dead until its last birth.

## 2. "Settled by construction"

- **Parts act alone, hence return for ever.** True, given the sameness lemma above, the stated closing-exception caveat (which is global through the never-used flag) and the knot bound.
- **Verdict fixed at birth.** True for connected structures. With the third bullet it also proves that every newborn passes. P6 of ticket A is therefore a theorem and tests only the code; the knot test can bite only under FLOOR0, the closing exception and PART-CLOSE.
- **r = f + 2p − 3 − 2e.** The algebra is right, and I checked it on rounds 1 and 2 (e = 2, 0, 2, 1). But e is read from the cluster, not from what the knot holds. So holdings give r only to within three values, and the owner's question is answered "no, to within 4" by construction.
- **The cohort law builds what the rounds build.** True by definition, since it is the round listed in a random order. Gate C(a) tests bookkeeping only.
- **B's bullets.** They make the gate "D2 and DW give the same roster" and most of B's P1 automatic: D2(n) is A's ring for odd n and half of Ring(2n).

## 3. Predictions

**The hand case: D2(5, 3) under L2 with DEPTH.**

1. Depth 0 completes as round 1 in any order: five joins J and five offshoots O, each with three fresh distinctions.
2. At depth 1, each J is in 4 open groups and holds 3, so it is short.
3. Each O is in 2 open groups, both containing a short J. It offshoots (3 → 2), offshoots again (2 → 1), and is then in 2 open groups holding 1, so it is short.
4. No O ever dies, so no J is ever freed. Depth 1 stops after exactly ten moves under any tie rule and under L1 as well.

So I disagree that offshoots-first reproduces the rounds. Joins-first "cannot" only vacuously: no join move ever exists at depth 1, and the forced J–O join appears only after a repair.

**If O is allowed to finish, two further failures follow.**
- A J freed early makes its offshoot and goes short. When it is freed again beside a short neighbour it holds 2 against one free group and can make a second offshoot. It then holds 1 against 2 open groups for good.
- Any J that offshoots before the last O dies holds 2, so no ring part the same as the start ever appears at any instant.

**Classification.**

| Verdict | Predictions |
| --- | --- |
| Likely false | A's gate (CAP-4 clause), A P8, C P3; C P6 is then moot |
| Trivially true | A P6; A P7's births and exception clauses; A P9 (neither added rule binds); B's gate; B P1; B P6; C gate (a); C P4 (vacuous); C P7 under RATION-3 |
| True for another reason | C P5: the first join always reads d = 2 and receives 2, so no part with three each can exist; order plays no role. L3 and L4 fail at depth 1 for the same reason |
| Real tests | A P1–P5 (replication), A P7's not-all-equal criterion, B P2, P3, P4, P5 |
| Confounded | C P1 and P2 (unbounded offshoot growth starves low depths before 800 moves); C P6 (the slowdown is the DEPTH scheduler's accounting, not the model) |

**The CAP-4 working.**
1. Under the ordinary law, the round-2 join of two joins is in one triple and four pairs, so it receives 5 (total fresh 55 = 15 + 40 spent in round 3).
2. Under CAP-4 it receives 4 and waits in round 3.
3. The five such knots form a cycle holding 4 each. From then on the joins have demand 6, receive 4 and wait, while the offshoots pair off and leave.
4. That cycle returns every two rounds from round 3. Check RATION-4 too.

## 4. Confounds and one control each

- **Artefacts.** Sameness is blind to the dead structure. Late returns are censored by the knot bound in A4 and by 10 rounds and 1,500 knots in B2. The comparison with the pilot shares the pilot's reading of the group rule.
- **A:** swap the release rule for "a member that is not short holds what its cancelled groups would take". I expect a permanent wait. Also freeze a hand trace of rounds 1 to 4 as a gate.
- **B:** P5 confounds deadness with meeting count (a dead knot needs three meetings) and with fewer members. Match each start with a dead knot against the same meeting pattern with that knot given one loose distinction.
- **C:** enumerate every tie order to depth 2 on D2(4, 3) instead of sampling 100 seeds, and add a deadlock outcome.

## 5. Known under other names

- **Iterated line graph.** The ordinary round on pair groups is this operator. Cycles are its only connected fixed points (van Rooij and Wilf, 1965), which is Ring(n, 2). The triple rule is a clique-graph variant (Prisner, *Graph Dynamics*).
- **Cycle space.** The parity test is the cycle space of the meeting multigraph with an outside vertex; a knot passes when it is not a cut vertex.
- **Boundary identity.** B's formula is the boundary count of a connected subtree: the sum of degrees less 2(size − 1).
- **Life and L-systems.** The two-rule ring is Life's breeder (quadratic growth), not its gun. The three-rule ring is a gun with eaters. The s + 2 chains are an L-system.
- **Confluence.** Critical pairs and local Church–Rosser in graph transformation (Ehrig, Plump); step against interleaving semantics in Petri nets; Kahn networks, where blocking reads give independence of schedule.

## 6. Words

- **ends:** five senses (the treatment, parts ending, a run ending, the two ends of a run of members, the records' growing end).
- **run:** an engine run, and a run of L members.
- **settled:** the section heading, and settled to depth D.
- **reference:** B's anchor, and C's comparison run.
- **witness:** this study's sense, the canonical test's quantified witnesses, and the standard certificate.
- **returns:** two definitions (rounds and serial), besides two older records' senses.
- **depth:** B's "In standard terms" uses it for the round. The two differ once knots wait (a ring join made in round 3 has depth 2).
- **age:** positive age of a roster, and "parts of one age".
- **cohort:** a round here, a depth in SERIAL-REPAIRS.
- **short, waits:** read once per round, but re-read per move in the serial law.
- **offshoot and bud:** two words for one thing. **Gives off, comes apart, emits, released:** four for one.
- **never used:** means barred; every loose distinction is literally never used.
- **adjacent:** in graph theory this is the program's "meet"; here it means two steps apart.
- **in balance:** suggests equilibrium, but the structure grows without bound, and under the two rules the ring is not in balance by its own definition.
- **ration, law:** each names both the kind and one member of it.
- **ring part:** a D2 start's ring part is a cycle, not a Ring.
